title: license payload
description: What a license file of elderlygate/mankit/license/v2 signs (license-file.schema.json's spec.payload, once decoded). nw-licenser writes it and mankit's licenses package reads it. Open (CT-RULE-4, ADR-S15).

kind.description: Which kind of license it is, so an app knows what it opens (ADR-L8). license: what the owner signs with nw-licenser for a person or an org; it opens the enterprise features it names (ADR-L2, L10). trial: the trial a product line carries built in; it opens every enterprise feature of its one app (ADR-L9).

for.description: The person or org the license names, never a machine, so whoever has the file sees whose it was (ADR-L4); for a trial, which names no one, its product line in words, for example "Acme 1"; never only spaces.

products.description: The enterprise feature ids the license names, per product id, so an app opens a feature only when its own product id names it (ADR-L2).

additionalProperties.description: The product's enterprise feature ids, each once, as its feature list names them.

lines.description: The product lines it opens, per product id, each by its number as the constitution's product-lines.yaml names it, so 1 is Designer 1 (V-10). An app opens what it names only while its own build's line is among them, and a later line needs a new license (ADR-L10).

additionalProperties.description: The product's line numbers, each once.

issued.description: The license's first day, an RFC 3339 date in UTC; it opens nothing before it.

until.description: The license's last day, an RFC 3339 date in UTC, never before issued; after it its features lock again (ADR-L3).

days.description: How long each trial it starts runs, in whole days, its first day counted, so every install of the product line's releases gets a trial of the same length (ADR-L9).

allOf.description: A license names one or more products, each with one or more feature ids, and has no days. It either runs until a day or names the lines it opens, never both (ADR-L10). When it names lines, they name exactly the products products names; no schema can say that, so mankit's license check keeps it (ADR-L2, L10).
A trial names no products and has no until: its trial offer does not end (ADR-L2, L9). Its lines name its one product and the one line it was signed for, and days how long its trials run (ADR-L9).

productId.description: A product id, the name the hubman catalog and every answer's source.app give the product (G-PLAN-12).

featureId.description: A product feature id, as the product's feature list names it, which is the one home of its ids (G-STACK-17): lowercase words joined by a hyphen, starting with a letter, at most 32 characters, like events, live-tracing or pdf-export. A license and a switch name a feature by it, so one form holds everywhere. A noun for what the feature is, never a tier or price word such as pro or premium; unique within its product; once released it never changes its meaning and is never reused. Only the form is this schema's to check.
